title: Medical Report Template: Free Examples & PDF Download [2026]
summary: Get a free medical report template with a worked example. See the standard 8-section format doctors use for insurance and legal reports.
body_text: A medical report template gives clinicians a standardized structure for documenting a patient's condition, findings, and treatment for insurers, lawyers, employers, and other providers. Below you'll find the complete medical report format, a copy-paste template, a fully worked example, and three free PDF downloads you can start using today. You can download the PDF version here . Key Takeaways Every medical report follows the same core structure: administrative details, clinician credentials, purpose, subjective findings, objective findings, opinion, and certification. Reports are legal documents, not clinical notes: unlike a progress note , a medical report is written for a third party and may be scrutinized in court or by an insurer. Templates cut writing time dramatically: a structured format means you fill in facts instead of composing prose from scratch for every request. AI can now draft reports for you: an AI medical scribe can pull the relevant history, investigations, and treatment timeline from your records and populate the template automatically. What Is a Medical Report Template? A medical report template is a pre-structured document that standardizes how a physician presents a patient's history, examination findings, diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis for an external audience. It typically includes fields for administrative details, the clinician's credentials, subjective and objective findings, a medical opinion, and a signed certification. A medical report is usually requested by someone outside the treating relationship (e.g. an insurance company, a lawyer, an employer, a government agency, or another specialist). That's what separates it from day-to-day chart documentation like SOAP or progress notes, which are written primarily for you and your care team. This means a medical report carries legal weight. It's an official statement of fact and professional opinion, and it needs to be accurate, complete, and defensible. The Standard Medical Report Format Formats vary slightly by country, specialty, and requesting organization, but virtually every medical report contains these eight sections in this order: Administrative details : Date of request, requesting party, claim or reference number, patient name and DOB, practice details. Clinician credentials : Your qualifications, years of experience, and your relationship to the patient (treating physician vs. independent examiner). Purpose and scope : Who requested the report, why, and what sources it's based on (records, examination, or both). Subjective findings : What the patient reports: symptoms, functional limitations, and impact on work and daily life. Objective findings : What the record shows: diagnoses with dates, investigation results, and treatment to date. Assessment and prognosis : Your clinical assessment, expected trajectory, and planned management. Medical opinion : Direct answers to the specific questions the requester asked. Certification and signature : A declaration that the report is true and correct, plus your signature, contact details, and date. Pro Tip: Before writing anything, re-read the request letter. Most rejected or returned reports fail because the clinician answered questions the requester never asked and skipped the ones they did. Medical Report Template (Copy & Paste) Here's the full blank template. Copy it into your EHR or word processor, or download it as a PDF . MEDICAL REPORT ADMINISTRATIVE DETAILS Date of request: Requested by (organization/individual): Claim/reference number: Patient name: Patient date of birth: Practice name: Clinician name and credentials: CLINICIAN DECLARATION This report has been prepared by [name], [qualifications], with [X] years of experience in [specialty]. I have been treating [patient] since [date] / I examined [patient] on [date] as an independent examiner. PURPOSE AND SCOPE This report was prepared at the request of [requester] regarding [condition/incident]. It is based on [medical records / clinical examination performed on date / both]. Any gaps in the available record are noted where relevant. SUBJECTIVE FINDINGS Demographic and contextual factors: Symptoms (patient-reported): Impact on work and daily living: OBJECTIVE FINDINGS History and diagnosis (with dates): Investigations and results: Treatment to date (medications, referrals, procedures): Ongoing/planned management: ASSESSMENT AND PROGNOSIS Current status: Expected course: Factors that may change the prognosis: MEDICAL OPINION / RESPONSES TO REQUESTED QUESTIONS [Answer each question from the request letter directly.] CERTIFICATION I certify that the information in this report is true and correct to the best of my knowledge. Clinician name and signature: Phone: Email: Date: Completed Medical Report Example Templates make more sense with a worked example. Here's the same structure filled out for a fictional workers' compensation request. Date of request: June 3, 2026 Requested by: Meridian Workers' Compensation Board Claim number: WC-2026-44172 Patient name: Sarah Chen Patient date of birth: February 14, 1974 Practice name: Lakeview Medical Group Clinician: Dr. James Okafor, MD, Family Medicine Clinician Declaration This report has been prepared by Dr. James Okafor, MD, with 15 years of experience in family medicine. I have been Ms. Chen's treating physician since 2018. Purpose and Scope This report was prepared at the request of the Meridian Workers' Compensation Board regarding Ms. Chen's right shoulder injury. It is based on her medical record and a clinical examination performed on May 28, 2026. Subjective Findings Ms. Chen is a 52-year-old dental hygienist whose work requires sustained overhead and reaching postures. She reports persistent right shoulder pain, worse with overhead activity, and night pain that disrupts sleep two to three times per week. She has taken approximately six weeks of medical leave since January 2026 and reports she cannot complete a full patient schedule without significant pain. Objective Findings First presentation: January 12, 2026, with right shoulder pain following a reaching injury at work. Diagnosis: Right rotator cuff tendinopathy with partial-thickness supraspinatus tear, confirmed February 2026. Ultrasound (February 2026): Partial-thickness articular-sided supraspinatus tear; no full-thickness tear. Treatment to date: Naproxen 500 mg twice daily as needed; corticosteroid injection (March 2026) with partial relief; physiotherapy twice weekly since February 2026, ongoing. Planned management: Continue physiotherapy; orthopedic review scheduled for September 2026; surgical opinion if conservative management fails. Assessment and Prognosis Ms. Chen's condition is improving slowly with conservative treatment. With continued physiotherapy and modified duties, I expect a functional recovery over six to nine months. Prognosis would worsen with a return to unrestricted overhead work at this stage. Medical Opinion Ms. Chen is currently fit for modified duties that avoid sustained overhead reaching and limit patient contact hours to six per day. She is not yet fit for her full pre-injury role. I recommend a workplace capacity review in three months. I certify that the information in this report is true and correct. I will provide a supplementary report if further detail is required. Signature: Dr. James Okafor, MD - (555) 214-8890 - j.okafor@lakeviewmedical.com - June 3, 2026 When You'll Need a Medical Report Medical report requests come from a handful of predictable sources. Knowing which one you're writing for changes what you emphasize. Insurance and Compensation Claims Insurers and compensation boards use your report to determine coverage, benefits, and return-to-work timelines. Focus on objective findings, functional capacity, and dates; vague language here delays claims and creates follow-up requests. Legal and Medico-Legal Matters In personal injury cases and other legal proceedings, your report may become evidence. Stick strictly to what the record supports, separate fact from opinion clearly, and never speculate beyond your expertise. Work Capacity and Disability Assessments Employers and government agencies need a clear answer to one question: what can this patient safely do? Spell out specific restrictions (weight limits, hours, movements) rather than general statements like "light duties." Referrals and Continuity of Care When another clinician requests a report, they need the clinical story fast: diagnosis, what's been tried, what worked, and what you want from them. The specialist referral template above is built for exactly this. How to Write a Medical Report in 5 Steps Read the request letter twice : List every question the requester asks. Your opinion section will answer these, in order. Gather the record : Pull diagnoses, investigation results, and treatment dates before you start writing. Chronology errors are the most common reason reports get challenged. Fill the template top to bottom : Keep subjective and objective findings strictly separated. "Patient reports" belongs in one section; "MRI showed" belongs in the other. Answer the questions directly : One clear paragraph per question. If you can't answer something from the available record, say so explicitly. Certify, sign, and keep a copy : Add your declaration, sign, and file the report in the patient's record. You may need it again for a supplementary request. A good medical report is boring in the best way: factual, chronological, and structured so the reader finds every answer exactly where they expect it. Common Medical Report Mistakes to Avoid Mixing fact and opinion: Keep patient-reported symptoms, documented findings, and your professional opinion in separate sections. Blurring them undermines the whole report's credibility. Missing dates: "Diagnosed with hypertension" is weak; "diagnosed with hypertension in March 2023" is defensible. Date everything. Copy-pasting clinical notes: Raw chart notes are full of abbreviations and internal shorthand a claims assessor won't understand. The report should translate the record, not reproduce it. Ignoring the certification: An unsigned or undeclared report is often legally invalid for the requester's purposes, which means you'll be writing it twice. That's the part worth automating. Sully.ai's AI Scribe captures every encounter as structured documentation, so when a report request lands, the clinical story is already organized. Point Sully at your template and it drafts the report from the existing record: you review, edit, and sign. Works with your templates: Use the templates on this page, your insurer's required format, or a custom one; Sully populates whichever structure you need, the same way it handles SOAP notes and progress notes. Lives inside your EHR: Deep integrations with Epic, Oracle Cerner, athenahealth, and dozens more mean no copy-pasting between systems. Built for compliance: HIPAA-compliant and encrypted end to end, with the clinician in control of every finished document. Frequently Asked Questions What is the difference between a medical report and a medical record? A medical record is the continuous, internal documentation of a patient's care over time. A medical report is a standalone document, written for a specific external requester, that summarizes and interprets the relevant parts of that record at a point in time. What should a medical report template include? At minimum: administrative details, clinician credentials, the purpose of the report, subjective findings, objective findings with dates, an assessment and prognosis, direct answers to the requester's questions, and a signed certification. How long does it take to write a medical report? With a template and an organized record, most routine reports take 20-45 minutes. Complex medico-legal reports can take several hours. Practices using an AI medical scribe cut this further because the clinical timeline is already structured when the request arrives. Can I charge for writing a medical report? Usually, yes. Reports requested by insurers, lawyers, and employers fall outside standard clinical care and are typically billed to the requesting party. Check the fee rules for your jurisdiction and the requesting organization before invoicing. Is a medical report legally binding? A medical report is a formal, certified statement that can be used as evidence in legal and administrative proceedings. That's why the certification section matters: you're declaring the contents true and correct, and inaccuracies can carry professional and legal consequences.

title: inBuild is the Bill.com for Procore
summary: Bill.com for Procore, giving contractors one place to capture, approve, code, and sync invoices without all the manual work.
body_text: If you have ever used Bill.com, you already understand the idea behind inBuild. Bill.com gave accounting teams one place to receive invoices, code bills, collect approvals, make payments, and sync everything with their accounting software. It took a process that lived in email, spreadsheets, and filing cabinets and turned it into a simple workflow. inBuild does the same thing for construction companies using Procore. The difference is that construction invoices are more complicated than normal bills. An invoice does not just need a vendor, invoice number, amount, and due date. It needs a project. It might need a purchase order or subcontract. It needs the right cost code, cost type, billing period, and schedule of values line. It also needs to reach the person who can confirm that the work was actually completed. That is where inBuild comes in. The problem is everything between the invoice and Procore Most construction companies already have the important systems in place. Procore manages the projects, budgets, commitments, and job costs. QuickBooks or another accounting system manages the general ledger and the company books. But there is still a lot of work required to move an invoice through those systems. An invoice comes into an email inbox. Someone downloads it, figures out which project it belongs to, finds the vendor in Procore, looks for the correct commitment, enters the line items, and sends it to the project manager for approval. Then they wait. If something is wrong, a new email thread starts. If the project manager forgets to respond, accounting has to follow up. Once the invoice is approved, someone may have to enter the same information into QuickBooks. The software is there, but the process between the systems is still manual. inBuild fills that gap. One place for every invoice inBuild gives your team one inbox for invoices, receipts, and other payable documents. Vendors can send invoices by email. Project managers can upload documents from the field. Accounting can see everything in one place instead of searching through individual inboxes or trying to figure out who received what. When an invoice arrives, inBuild reads it and uses the data already in Procore to help identify the project, vendor, commitment, and cost code. Your team reviews the information, makes any changes, and sends the invoice through the approval process. Once it is approved, inBuild syncs it into Procore. If you use the QuickBooks integration, it can also flow into your accounting system. The goal is simple. Enter the information once, review it, approve it, and let the systems stay in sync. Built around the way contractors work This is where the Bill.com comparison really makes sense. Bill.com understands a normal accounts payable workflow. inBuild understands a construction accounts payable workflow. It knows that the same vendor may work across several projects. It knows that an invoice may need to be applied against a purchase order or subcontract. It knows the difference between a commitment invoice and a direct cost. It works with the projects, vendors, budgets, commitments, and cost codes that already exist in Procore. That context matters. A general accounts payable tool can read the amount on an invoice. A construction accounts payable tool needs to understand where that amount belongs inside the project. Without that connection, accounting still has to do the hard part manually. Approvals without the constant follow up Approvals are another big part of the process. Every contractor handles them differently. Some invoices go to a project manager. Larger invoices may also need approval from an executive. Direct costs may follow a different process than subcontractor invoices. inBuild lets companies create approval workflows that match how their teams already operate. Invoices can be routed based on the project, amount, cost code, or type of cost. Everyone can see where an invoice is in the process. Comments stay with the invoice. Accounting knows who needs to take action without digging through email threads. It is a small change that makes a big difference, especially when you are processing hundreds of invoices every month. Procore stays at the center inBuild is not trying to replace Procore. Procore should remain the source of truth for your project financials. That is where your budgets, commitments, changes, and job costs belong. inBuild simply makes it easier to get accurate information into Procore. It handles the work that happens before an invoice becomes a clean financial record. It receives the document, helps code it, routes it for approval, and syncs it to the systems that need it. Procore manages the project. QuickBooks manages the books. inBuild manages the accounts payable process between them. Why this matters Manual invoice entry is annoying, but wasted time is only part of the problem. When invoices sit in inboxes, project budgets are not current. When coding is rushed, costs end up in the wrong place. When approvals happen through scattered emails and text messages, nobody has a clear view of what is still outstanding. Those problems make it harder to understand what a project actually costs. inBuild gives accounting and operations one shared process. Accounting gets cleaner data and better visibility. Project managers can review costs without becoming data entry clerks. Leadership gets a more accurate picture of payables across the company. Most importantly, fewer invoices fall through the cracks. The Bill.com experience, built for Procore Bill.com showed businesses that accounts payable could be much easier. inBuild is bringing that same experience to construction. It gives Procore users one place to receive, code, review, approve, and sync invoices. It understands the financial structure behind every project, so your team spends less time moving information between systems and more time using that information to make decisions. That is why we call inBuild the Bill.com for Procore. It is accounts payable automation built around the way contractors actually work. Ready to see it in action? Learn more about inBuild .

title: Lam Research and NY Creates Team Up to Enable Training of University Students for the Semiconductor Workforce
summary: Lam's Semiverse ® Solutions virtual fabrication platform expected to provide hands-on chip fabrication training for engineering students across NY Creates' workforce development network News Summary
body_text: Lam's Semiverse ® Solutions virtual fabrication platform expected to provide hands-on chip fabrication training for engineering students across NY Creates' workforce development network News Summary Lam Research and NY Creates will collaborate to advance semiconductor workforce development across the northeastern United States. The program is expected to enable training of up to approximately 3,500 students over five years through scaled deployment at colleges and universities across the NY Creates workforce development ecosystem. Lam intends to provide access to its Semiverse® Solutions virtual process fabrication software, SEMulator3D®, along with lab materials and curriculum development support. NY Creates will coordinate program delivery across its partner institutions and align with regional workforce and advanced manufacturing initiatives. The collaboration supports the National Network for Microelectronics Education Northeast and broader state and regional semiconductor workforce goals. FREMONT, Calif. and ALBANY, N.Y. , Aug. 12, 2026 / PRNewswire / -- Lam Research Corp . (Nasdaq: LRCX) and New York Center for Research, Economic Advancement, Technology, Engineering and Science ( NY Creates ) today announced a collaboration to enable the training of approximately 3,500 students in semiconductor process integration over the next five years. NY Creates is a New York not-for-profit organization that owns and operates the Albany NanoTech Complex, the most advanced nonprofit-led 300mm semiconductor R&D site in North America. The program will use Lam's SEMulator3D® virtual fabrication software, part of the Semiverse ® Solutions portfolio, to deliver hands-on learning across NY Creates' network of partner colleges and universities in the Northeast. Addressing a Critical Talent Gap The semiconductor industry faces a growing talent shortage as next-generation chip technologies demand engineers with hands-on process integration experience — which many universities cannot provide because of the high cost of physical fabrication facilities, equipment, and materials. This collaboration bridges that gap directly, bringing industry-grade virtual fabrication tools into academic programs at scale, without requiring access to a cleanroom. "Preparing the next generation of semiconductor engineers requires more than classroom instruction; students need practical experience with the complex process decisions that shape how advanced chips are made," said David Fried, chief AI officer and corporate vice president for Semiverse Solutions at Lam Research. "Through this collaboration, access to Lam's SEMulator3D virtual fabrication platform is expected to help students build the critical process integration skills that complex chipmaking demands before they set foot in a fab." SEMulator3D is a semiconductor process modeling platform that uses advanced physics-based simulation to virtually replicate fabrication steps such as etch, deposition, and lithography for the full virtual fabrication flow, enabling students to design, analyze, and optimize chip manufacturing integration flow without the need for physical wafers. By visualizing how individual process steps interact — and the tradeoffs involved in building advanced semiconductor structures — students can move beyond learning what happens in chip manufacturing to understanding why specific process decisions are made. Integrating SEMulator3D into engineering curricula can accelerate the learning process and instill a deeper understanding of the complexities and nuances of manufacturing semiconductor chips at current and future technology nodes. "Lam Research's Semiverse Solutions bring world-class virtual fabrication capabilities directly into our partner institutions," said Dr. Robert Geer, NY Creates Vice President for Education and Workforce Development. "This collaboration enables students across the Northeast to access immersive, hands-on learning that directly prepares them for careers in advanced semiconductor manufacturing — and strengthens the regional talent pipeline that our ecosystem needs." Scale and Scope of the Program The collaboration is expected to advance semiconductor workforce development across NY Creates' programs and partner colleges and universities, using academic partnerships and industry-aligned education in advanced semiconductor manufacturing and process integration. Specifically, the program is intended to: Expand curriculum: Develop semiconductor process integration coursework aligned to advanced logic technologies and modern fabrication flows. Enable virtual learning at scale: Use SEMulator3D to deliver hands-on learning in complex device architectures across the NY Creates workforce development network to reach college and university students. Support regional workforce goals: Align with state and regional initiatives, including the National Network for Microelectronics Education (NNME) Northeast, supporting next-generation semiconductor manufacturing. As the Regional Node lead for NNME, NY Creates helps coordinate regional collaboration and industry alignment efforts across the broader Northeast ecosystem. About Lam Research Lam Research Corporation is a global supplier of innovative wafer fabrication equipment and services to the semiconductor industry. Lam's equipment and services allow customers to build smaller and better performing devices. In fact, today nearly every advanced chip is built with Lam technology. We combine superior systems engineering, technology leadership, and a strong values-based culture, with an unwavering commitment to our customers. Lam Research (Nasdaq: LRCX) is a FORTUNE 500® company headquartered in Fremont, Calif., with operations around the globe. Learn more at www.lamresearch.com . About NY Creates NY Creates serves as a lab-to-fab bridge for advanced electronics, fostering public-private and industry-academic partnerships for technology development and innovation. Creates attracts and leads industry-connected innovation and commercialization projects that secure significant investment, advance R&D in emerging technologies, and generate the jobs of tomorrow. Creates runs some of the most advanced facilities in the world, boasts more than 2,700 industry experts and faculty, and manages public and private investments of $25 billion—placing it at the global epicenter of high-tech innovation and commercialization.
